about: The release records of graview.dev: one per version in packages/core/CHANGELOG.md, newest first, written with the Version packages pull request. A version npm never got says which version carried it (shippedIn) and is said inside that version's section. The date is the day npm published it (UTC). tests/the-releases-page-says-what-each-version-brought.test.ts fails while a version in the changelog has no record here.

releases.headline: Several people type into one long text field at once and keep every word: over the wire, in the editor, in words, whatever the network does.
releases.summary:
- **Over the wire.** `remote.typing(node, field)` sends a field's typing a run at a time as `type-text`, and the server carries each run over everyone else's, so two pages typing into one field both keep their words, over the socket or the poll. A reader that never said it reads op format 3 is sent the whole text instead of a splice. `@graview/core/typing` loads the first time somebody types.
- **In the editor.** Prose the declaration types together opens with no draft and no Save: each keystroke is the field's at once, somebody else's typing lands as it arrives with the selection carried over it, and Ctrl or ⌘ Z takes back only this person's own last run. Presence carries a caret.
- **In words.** A run of typing is said as what it wrote, where and how much ("Ada wrote in Kitchen's notes (+42 −3)"): one tick in the timeline, one row in Activity with one undo, one notification when the typist stops, and `historyInWords` for an agent's history.
- **Whatever the network does.** A seeded fuzz of three pages typing, with frames held, duplicated and lost and runs taken back at random, found five ways an undo of typing went wrong; all are fixed.
releases.compatibility: `transformSplices`, `composeSplices`, `diffSplice` and `isCollaborativeField` move from `@graview/core` to `@graview/core/typing`. A `type-text` behind the horizon is answered `conflict` where it was refused `invalid`; a whole write over a field typed together may now be refused as stale by a server before 0.1.50. `LiveProtocol` gains `floor(peers)`, so a host's own implementation has one more method to write. A notification's field typed into carries `typed` (`{ inserted, removed, spans }`) instead of `before` and `after`. Additive: presence `caret`, the provider's `typing`, `EmbedRemote.typing`, `historyInWords` and the typing words, `holdTypingRuns` and `typingQuietMs`, `StoreHandler.pins()` and `compact`. Ops, stored formats and `WIRE_PROTOCOL` are unchanged.

releases.headline: The 1.0 foundations: formats that fail closed, links with ids of their own, opaque cursors, a publishing lifecycle, and the first two phases of text typed together.
releases.summary:
- **Formats fail closed.** A primitive, a typed value or a store format a build does not know is refused with `NewerFormatError` rather than skipped; an author kind it does not know reads as the system's; a refusal code a client does not know is final. Two writers on one log fail loudly with `LogHeadMovedError` instead of writing a second op 1.
- **Links, ids and cursors.** A link may carry an `id` and `data` of its own; an act honors a caller's id when it is free and refuses one that is taken; a page's own ids travel as a hint, so two people adding the same name both land. Positions on the wire are opaque cursors.
- **Publishing.** Under `publishing: { mode: "on-publish" }`, collaborators edit live and everyone else reads the app as of the last `publish`; `?as=published` shows what readers see, and `unpublished(store)` says what is waiting.
- **Text typed together.** A text field takes a `splice-text`, transformed so concurrent typing converges; the `type-text` act in `@graview/core/typing` merges keystrokes, an agent's whole rewrite and undo out of order.
- **Not now.** The Suggested tray hides a suggestion from one person until tomorrow, and a night's tidying is one row in Activity.
releases.compatibility: Stored formats: op format 3 — a store this build writes is refused by an earlier one with `NewerFormatError`, so roll back by refolding from the log. The wire: positions are cursor strings on `welcome`, `ack`, `ops`, `/graview/state`, `/graview/since` and `/graview/here`; a server reads a page's old number for one minor. A caller's `id` with a space, over 200 characters, or naming a record the act did not make is refused. A visitor form's ops say author kind `visitor`. `appendOps` takes `{ head }`, and an adapter that ignores it works as before. Additive: edge `id`/`data`, `mintedHint`, `publishing`, `publish`, `servedThrough`, `Store.servedSeq`, `CompactOptions.pins`, `unauthenticated` and `quota`, `collaborative` on a document field, `Dismissal`, `withNotNow`.

releases.headline: An app tidies itself overnight, judged by a model where one is lent; suggestions and lineage take their 1.0 shapes; every form asks in one order.
releases.summary:
- **Dreaming.** `@graview/tools/tidy` gives an app its own actor: `dream()` finds candidates in code and, where the host lends a System One model such as Jev, asks it whether two records are the same thing, which record a field means, whether a record is finished, and which choice fits an empty field. What it is sure of may apply where the host allows; the rest waits as suggestions; without a model, rules do the judging. `whileAway()` says what happened since a person last looked; `suggest_changes` lets a remote actor suggest; `graview dream` runs it from the command line.
- **Suggestions and lineage, as 1.0 keeps them.** A suggestion may expire; "not now" is one person's and leaves it waiting for everyone else; a decline answers by meaning, so the same change asked another way stays declined. Lineage names the run, the judge and the evidence, and keeps keys a later build adds.
- **The model door takes an object.** `Completion` takes `{ prompt, system, images, signal }` and answers `{ text, usage }`; the Fast slot's types live in their own module; the seat's offers are `Offer`.
- **Every form asks in one order**, whatever declared it: the label's fields, then what is required, then the rest. A declaration may name an act in another spelling.
- **Smaller things.** Enter in Find leaves the box in the same press; a wider focus ring stays whole at a view's edge; `graview view check --audit --browser` runs every accessibility rule in Chromium; the host learns what a view hears a click on.
releases.compatibility: `Completion` changes shape (an object in, `{ text, usage }` out) and `Suggestion`/`suggestionsFor` in `@graview/tools/suggest` are renamed `Offer`/`offersFor`. Additive: `@graview/tools/tidy`, the `suggest_changes` tool for automated seats, a suggestion's `expiresAt`, lineage's `run`, `actor` and `evidence` (and unknown keys kept), declines matched by meaning, `Dismissal`. A document's act arguments and every generated form ask in a new order. Ops, stored formats and the wire are otherwise unchanged.

releases.headline: Forms ask the name first, acts answer to the way they're spelled, refusals name the act that would, and a place says its forms.
releases.summary:
- **A creating form asks the name first.** Then the required fields, then the rest, in the page's order, whatever order the document keeps its fields in. A key's abbreviation is said as its letters: `cvss` is "CVSS", `sourceUrl` "Source URL".
- **An act answers to its other spellings.** `connect-threat-partOf` runs `connect-threat-part-of`; a name no act has is answered with the nearest one. A relation from a kind to itself is titled from its description: "Set the family it belongs to".
- **Refusals name the act that would.** An edit refused a field another act writes says which act: "whatToDo is set by set-verdict". A number given as its digits ("8.6") is read as the number.
- **Capitals where they belong.** A headline that opens on a count in words starts with a capital; an acronym ("CVEs") is never lowered.
- **A declared row names its record** when its blocks don't, so the picture and its words agree.
- **describe_place says a place's forms**: each creating act's fields in order, required, with their choices; and a visitor form at `forms/<name>`.
- **A hidden lens is hidden where a record is seen**, and a title another lens holds is refused by naming that lens. A draft view takes no title a titled view already has.
releases.compatibility: Additive in the API: `actSpelledAs`, `nearestAct`, `numbersSpelled`, `capitalize` and `lowerFirst` on `@graview/core/words`, `blocksName` on `/blocks`, `DescribedForm` on `/describe`, `views` on `DraftOptions` and `DraftTools`. A document's creating acts take their arguments in a new order (name, then required, then the rest), so a generated form and an agent tool's schema list them so; a field's label for a known abbreviation changes ("Id" is "ID"); a number argument given as an exact numeric string is accepted where it was refused. Ops, stored formats and the wire are unchanged.

releases.headline: Custom views work by keyboard with real links and buttons, are as tall as they draw, and can be audited for accessibility; a place is said drawn once its lens has drawn.
releases.summary:
- **Views work by keyboard by default.** A control a view draws is reached by Tab and pressed by Enter and Space without scrolling the page; whatever has the keyboard shows a ring a view can restyle but not remove; `.graview-sr` is words for a screen reader alone; an unlabeled `<svg>` is hidden from one; focus stays on a keyed element across a render.
- **Real `<a>` and `<button>`.** Both start as plain words a view styles freely; `<button data-record>` goes where it says; `a[data-record]` and `a[data-place]` carry a real `href`, so a new tab, a middle click and copy link work. An embed that keeps its own addresses hands them in with `hrefOf`.
- **A view is as tall as it draws.** The host measures it. On Pages it flows with the page; on the Scene a view of many or of one record is a card held to its box, faded where there is more, with Open (or Expand where there are no pages). `flows: false` and `scene.maxHeight` are new in the manifest.
- **An accessibility audit of a drawn view.** `auditView` on `@graview/guest/audit`, `graview view check --audit`, and `audit: true` on a headless run: keyboard reach, names, state, nesting, images, scroll boxes, and in a browser the focus ring and contrast, each against its WCAG 2.2 criterion.
- **Checks know a view's place.** A link to a titled view's place is no longer flagged as going nowhere when the host hands the check its views, and `describePlace` describes such a place.
- **A place is said drawn once its lens has drawn.** `data-graview-drawn` and `onDrawn` wait for a declared lens's rows, so `graview shots` and `graview preview` no longer photograph a blank place; a full-page shot shows the whole of a long place.
- **Find hands the keyboard to a place at once.** Enter on a kind in Find no longer leaves the keyboard in the Find box while the place's line is still coming, where the next key a person typed went on a slow machine.
releases.compatibility: Additive in the manifest (`flows`, `scene.maxHeight`) and the API (`auditView`, `GoTo.href`, `hrefOf` on the embed and `PagesApp`, `lazyPart`, `PartsWatch`, `viewPlaceOf`, `views` on `runWorkerViewHeadless`). A view's links now carry an `href` and lose the role and tab stop the host added; buttons and host links are reset to their words at zero specificity; Enter and Space on a pressable element are heard as a click; a one-record view on the Scene is a card rather than scrolling inside its box; a framed place's scroll box takes the keyboard and is named. `data-graview-drawn` comes later than before, when a lens draws. Ops, stored formats and the wire are unchanged.

releases.headline: Built-in views share one type scale and one heading per page, a view's own place flows with the page, and the home may keep the line under the name off.
releases.summary:
- **Built-in views look designed.** Place headers, blocks lenses, grouped lists, kind lists and record pages share one type scale, one left edge and one heading. A lens's headline becomes the line under the page's title instead of a second heading; a group's heading is its label and its count; a record's name in a row or card is set in the text face; choices in a line of facts are drawn as small chips; spacing follows a 4px scale, given as `--graview-space-1` … `--graview-space-7`.
- **A view's place flows with the page.** A titled worker view at `/places/<slug>` is no longer drawn in a fixed-height frame that scrolls inside itself, which trapped the thumb on a phone. A calendar, a board and the other pictures keep their frame.
- **The home may keep its line off.** `brand.subtitle: false` keeps the description from being drawn under the app's name on the home, so a home view with its own hero no longer says everything twice. The description stays the app's, in its listings and on the name's hover.
releases.compatibility: Additive in the declaration: `brand.subtitle`, optional and only `false`; a build that predates it refuses a document that carries it. Additive in the API: `Brand.subtitleDrawn`, the `set-brand` edit's `subtitle`, `PlacePageHead` on `@graview/primitives/pages`, `runs` on a resolved text block whose facts name a choice field, `count` on a grouped list's group in `describe_place`, and the `--graview-space-*` tokens. A titled worker view's place no longer scrolls inside itself. Ops, stored formats, the wire and the derived tools are unchanged.

releases.headline: A form for a visitor, cards that open on a phone's tap, and views that link out, bleed and stack their stylesheets.
releases.summary:
- **A form for a visitor.** An app can declare a form — one act drawn alone for somebody with no account — whose answer lands as a record and shows nothing else of the app. `@graview/embed/form` mounts it anywhere.
- **A card opens on a tap.** Any element a view binds to a record or a place opens it on a click, a phone's tap and Enter, from wherever inside it the press lands. Any element bound to an act presses as a button does, and a headless run can press it and say what it would send.
- **Views link out, safely.** A view may link to an address a record it was shown holds, drawn to open in a new tab with no referrer; an address the view built is refused, so a link cannot carry what the view read.
- **Every stylesheet is drawn.** A view that calls `graview.style` twice draws both, in order.
- **A view can go edge to edge on a phone** with `bleed: true`, and a record page draws its slot under a view that does not replace the page.
- **The keyboard goes where an act asks**, and the undo key the offer names is the one the journeys press.
releases.compatibility: The `style` message between a view's runtime and its host carries `sheets` where it carried `css`, and `HeadlessTranscript.css` is `sheets`; the two ship together in `@graview/guest`. An element other than an `<a>` bound to a record, and one other than a button bound to an act, now opens or presses and is given `tabindex` and a role; a text field or select with `data-act` and no `data-save` no longer presses. `forms` is a new key in the declaration and the document. `bleed` is new in the manifest; `links` on a worker view's options; `describePlace` takes `views`. Under a view that sits above the page, a fact the page's blocks say is not listed again.

releases.headline: A compacted store shows a seat only what it may see, history judged for one seat, and views that stand in the nav.
releases.summary:
- **A security fix for compacted stores.** A store opened from a checkpoint could serve a seat the id of a record removed before the checkpoint, inside a field of a record the seat may see. The checkpoint now keeps what it needs to judge that, and an older checkpoint fails closed.
- **History judged for one seat.** `archivedSeenBy` serves a range of the archive, with its checkpoints, as one seat may see it.
- **A view stands in the nav.** A view the host keeps can be ordered among the places and opened first; a kind kept off the places leaves the Pages drop-down and stays reachable at its address.
- **The two-scheme logo** has a capability id and one public reader.
- **The Nightly's engines leg looks twice** before it fails, and keeps its verdicts.
releases.compatibility: Checkpoints gain `removed` and `writers` (optional; older builds ignore them); a store opened on an older checkpoint fails closed for a seat whose sight is not total, so a host mends each once. `view:<name>` in `pages.order`, `first` and `primary`; `editDocument`, `compileDocument` and `placesOf` take `views`; a kind in `pages.hide` leaves the bar's places. About 2 KB more up front.

releases.headline: A change carries its value once less: smaller histories for every app.
releases.summary:
- **A saved change no longer keeps its own undo copy.** It was always worked out from what changed; now it is worked out when undo, playback or a rebase needs it, instead of being stored and sent. An image field's change is about 40% smaller, and a whole history of image edits about 38%.
- **Nothing old breaks.** A store written by an earlier version opens and carries on; exports from earlier versions import and undo the same; a tab on an earlier version is still sent each change with its undo copy written out.
releases.compatibility: Op format 2: ops carry no `inverse` (read it with `inverseOf(op)`); `AppendOp.inverse` is gone. A version before 0.1.43 that opens a store or export written by this one refuses it with `NewerFormatError`. A reader says it reads format 2 on the wire (`opFormat`); one that says nothing gets format 1. About 0.5 KB more up front.

releases.headline: Pages that say where you are, a logo for each scheme, gestures in views, an open on a short tail, and playback past the undo horizon.
releases.summary:
- **A page says where you are.** A derived list, record or picture opens with a "You are here" trail; `usePlaceHere()` and `registry.section` let a design's own shell light its tab.
- **Undo and Find fit a design's bar.** `<PageUndo compact />`, and `className` and `size` on both.
- **A logo for each scheme.** `brand.logo: { light, dark? }`, drawn in the dark by the bar and `AppMark`; a light logo inverted only when the brand asks.
- **Worker views hear wheel, drag and pinch** when their manifest says `gestures: true`.
- **Heavy apps open fast.** A page can open on the snapshot and a short tail of the log (`openTail`), and a view's code is fetched only when it is drawn.
- **Playback reaches past the undo horizon** by asking the host's archive for the older changes.
- **The framework costs half as much to import** in a Worker: schemas are built on first use and zod is shaken to what is called.
- **A recipe:** a product face of its own over a running preview.
releases.compatibility: `Brand.logo` is `string | BrandLogo` (read `logoOf(brand)?.light`); a host building its own `Playback` sets `archive: null`; the exported document shapes are `z.lazy`; a field revision is stale only when written after the claim; `openTail`, `HistoryHost.archived` and a lazy `worker` are additive. About 3 KB more up front.

releases.headline: The app bar holds still at every width.
releases.summary: - **The app bar no longer flickers.** At some widths the places in the bar stood, squeezed the app's name onto two lines, folded, and stood again, over and over. Whether they stand, and whether the Scene and Pages switch shows its words, is now weighed with the name as it stands on one line, and the room before Find is measured as it is drawn.
releases.compatibility: A place near the bar's edge may now fold where it stood, because the row is no longer weighed 8 px roomier than it is. About 0.5 KB more up front.

releases.headline: Edits kept the moment they are made, labels that keep their space in a focused scene, a keyboard that reaches what it means, and a first draw with no extra round trips.
releases.summary:
- **Stores persist in IndexedDB.** A page's store moves from localStorage to IndexedDB, carried forward intact, so a large one survives in Safari; every edit is journaled the moment it is made, so leaving the page loses nothing.
- **A focused scene gives its words room.** Relation headings sit over their own cards, counts appear once per district, and lines route around labels.
- **The keyboard reaches what it means.** Skip links into a long list, the chosen card and the problems; a menu of acts is one Tab stop. Keyboard presses across the examples' jobs fell from 1,995 to 1,103.
- **The first draw needs no extra round trips.** `firstDrawChunks` names what a face's first paint opens, and early fetches wait for it.
- **Smaller asks:** a drop takes the photo's capture time; the scene opens on the overview and can sit under a host's own bar; `sync-seed`'s dry run refuses what the apply would; `graview preview` stops when told; `graview check` warns of long headlines and templates in code describes; `shots` and `preview` take an app declared in code.
- **Apps that run the framework from source take their aliases from its exports** (`sourceAliases`), including projects `graview create --link` makes.
releases.compatibility: The browser adapter keeps stores in IndexedDB (localStorage stores are carried forward) and `loadMeta`/`saveMeta` return promises; the adapter journals ops (`journal`, `loadJournal`); `mount`'s `bar` takes `{ faces?: false, name?: false }`; the scene with no path opens on the overview (`where().stop` is `#overview=1`); `spatialHref(id, sceneHref)`; `sync-seed` exits 1 on a seed the declaration refuses; `ServedStore.close({ grace })`; new check findings `describe-template-in-code`, `view-headline-long`, `lens-column-written-unsaid`. The hosted page carries about 2 KB more up front.

releases.headline: Cards that answer the menu under a base, full-size photos in views, views that save as you type and take a drop, and a page that says when it has drawn.
releases.summary:
- **Cards answer the right-click menu on a hosted page.** A board or blocks card served under a base path offers its acts and Move to ›, a new tab keeps the base, and a finger resting on a board card opens its menu, so a phone moves cards again.
- **Full-size photos in views.** A view that shows record pictures draws them at any size, and the headless check says when a page would leave one out.
- **Views save as you type.** A field marked `data-save="input"` saves when the person pauses, and the view hears whether it saved.
- **Drop photos and videos onto a view.** A view marks where files may land; the host takes them, stores them and makes one record per file, in one undoable change, with a picker on a phone.
- **The page says when it has drawn.** `data-graview-drawn` and `onDrawn` replace a timer for anyone picturing a place, and a page can open on a view proposed and not yet kept.
- **add-lens refuses an option the lens does not take.**
- **Authoring skills split at their limit**, so each teaches one job.
releases.compatibility: `mount` takes `onDrawn(place)` (the old first-commit callback is `onFaceDrawn` on `<Embed>`), `draftView` and `handle.setDraftView`; `@graview/embed` depends on `@graview/guest`; `add-lens` refuses an unknown option (`lens-option-unknown`, an error) and `lensOptionsRefused` judges a patch; a worker view's manifest takes `accepts`, and `graview.act` takes a list of arguments as one change; a board card's long press opens its menu; code acts that move a board's cards need `sets` (`lens-column-written-unsaid`). The hosted page carries about 4 KB more up front.

releases.headline: Boards without buttons that search and filter, places that hide and restore views, a menu that offers what exists, and the last of inline AI.
releases.summary:
- **Boards without buttons.** A card moves by drag, by the keyboard or from its menu's Move to, with no Move button under every card, and a board takes search, filter and column options, showing search by itself once it is big.
- **Places that tidy their views.** Right-click a place to hide or delete a view; Hidden and Recently deleted (kept 30 days) sit at the foot of the places list.
- **A menu that offers what exists.** Before drawing a new view, the right-click menu offers the one the app already has.
- **The last of inline AI.** Several records chosen get suggestions for the set, one quiet hover chip can offer the likeliest next step, and the menu's AI part fills in well under 400 ms.
- **graview.dev shows the interface is generated, then reshaped by asking.**
releases.compatibility: A columns lens draws no Move button unless `move: true`; lenses take `options`; `keptViews` on `mount`, the provider and the Shell, with `/graview/views` and `remoteViews`; `ai.hoverChips` (off by default); places carry `lens`, `reads`, `name` and `declared`. The hosted page carries about 2.7 KB more up front.

releases.headline: Times in the app's own time zone, acts for every relation, video on records, and lines that wait for a view that draws late.
releases.summary:
- **Times in the app's zone.** An app says its time zone once; lists, record pages, act answers and views say times there, `{at | time}` and `{at | datetime}` read them out, and a rule's `today()` turns at the app's midnight.
- **Every relation can be linked.** Each relation comes with its own connect and disconnect acts, so an app can link two records without writing an act for it.
- **Video on records.** A video field plays on a record's page, and a view can place a host-drawn player and a full-screen viewer.
- **Lines that wait.** A view that draws its members late, as on a slow phone, still gets its lines.
- **The twelfth walk** (a film festival at real size) found seven problems, all fixed, among them a date editor that refused a stored time, a repair offered and then refused, and records of one name told apart by their ids.
releases.compatibility: `brand.timeZone`, `timeZone` on the provider, `mount` and `PageContext`; derived `connect-<kind>-<relation>` and `disconnect-<kind>-<relation>` acts appear in act lists and tool surfaces, and `edge-without-severer` is no longer reported; a `video` field type; `seenBy` is generic over the store. The hosted page carries about 7 KB more up front.

releases.headline: A record's pictures load under the host's base on every face, and a view draws the pictures and app images it was promised.
releases.summary:
- **Pictures load where the host serves them.** An app served under a path (`/a/<app>/`) drew its records' pictures and documents from the site's root; `HostFiles.src` now says where, and `filesAt` works it out from its own address, so a host that already uses it needs no change.
- **Views get their pictures.** A view that asks for pictures receives each image's `src`, live and in a preview, and a picture the host doesn't answer for is said with what the host answered.
- **Views draw the app's own images in every form** they are written in, and a refusal only offers what the host actually draws.
releases.compatibility: `HostFiles` takes `src`; `fileSrc` on `@graview/core`; views take `file`; `runWorkerViewHeadless` takes `asset` and `origin`; `sayRefusal` takes the host's `{ origins, assets }`. The guest host's first load is about 0.4 KB larger.

releases.headline: A relation to another app can be made by an edit, a host may say later whether it still keeps a file, and playback asks for a past declaration when it gets there.
releases.summary:
- **A cross-app relation from an edit.** The `add-relation` edit, the studio and anything that sends edits can now relate a kind to another app's kind (`"to": ["@nick/house/house"]`), refused with the checker's own words when it can't be. Migrations no longer drop such a relation's links.
- **Files a host answers for later.** `HostFiles.kept` may return a promise: a picture is drawn as itself until the host answers, then as removed later if it was, and each file is asked once.
- **Past declarations on demand.** Playback asks the host for a past version's declaration when it reaches it (`declarationAt`), so a page no longer carries every version up front.
releases.compatibility: `add-relation` accepts a `to` of `"@<address>/<kind>"`. `HostFiles.kept` may return `Promise<boolean>`. `HistoryHost` takes `declarationAt`. Nothing breaks; the hosted page carries about 0.5 KB more up front.

releases.headline: The right-click menu tells a visitor how to get in, draws a panel where it was asked, spends no thinking-model call on opening, and is ready before the click.
releases.summary:
- **A visitor is told how to get in.** A host passes `signIn` while nobody is signed in; a reader who may do nothing sees one sign-in row in the menu and at a list's foot instead of every act struck through, and is not offered Notify me.
- **A panel drawn from the menu stays on its face.** On Pages, "Draw a panel" opens the draft page with Keep as a lens and Discard; over the scene the draft is framed as a panel; a failed ask is said in the menu.
- **Opening a menu costs nothing.** With only a thinking model, suggestions wait for a "Suggest…" press; with a Fast slot they are asked once per record until it changes.
- **The menu is ready before the click.** Resting on a record, focusing it or touching it prepares its menu, so it opens complete.
- **The eleventh walk** (an animal shelter at real size) found six problems, all fixed: finding a past record by name, filtering a status board, offered repairs that were refused, a misnamed heading, Tab from a chosen box, and the scaffold's own test under a policy.
releases.compatibility: `mount`, `<Embed>`, `GraviewProvider` and `PageContext` take `signIn` (`SignIn` from `@graview/core`). `HostAi.suggestOnOpen` is new; with only a thinking slot the menu no longer suggests as it opens. The hosted page carries about 0.2 KB more up front.

releases.headline: A read-only calendar takes its own changes under a policy, and a host keeps Notify me in its own store.
releases.summary:
- **A read-only connection works under a policy.** A calendar the app only reads now brings its own changes in when the app declares who may do what, and a change the app refuses is reported as refused rather than as the calendar being unreachable.
- **Notify me on a hosted page.** `mount` takes the host's subscription store, so subscriptions made from the right-click or a record page are kept by the host on both faces; keeping them that way adds no parser to the first load, about 9.4 KB less than before.
releases.compatibility: `SyncReport.refused` may now name an inbound change (`SyncRefusal`, with the remote `resource` and `id`), and `offline` is true only when the remote itself fails. `mount` and `<Embed>` take `subscriptions`.

releases.headline: Ask with ⌘K and the right-click, be told when things happen, a faster first load, the GPU by default, and a Google calendar kept in step.
releases.summary:
- **The AI where you are working.** ⌘K opens a bar beside what you're on that completes its acts, places and records; anything else is asked, and the answer is a card beside the record or list. The right-click offers suggestions, fills, new records and panels, picked only from what you may see and do. Every proposed change is previewed first, accepted all or some, and undone in one step, and Activity keeps each AI interaction.
- **Notify me.** Subscribe to an act, a kind or a record in two presses from a right-click, a record page or chat. A change by someone else that you may see tells the host once.
- **Faster.** First load to interactive is 31–38% faster on a desk and on a slowed phone, held by a CI budget, and the scene draws on the GPU where the browser can, with unfocused planes blurred.
- **Dates and calendars.** One date and date-time editor everywhere that reads "tomorrow 3pm" or "Fri 10:30" and shows times in your zone. A Google calendar can be declared in the app (a calendar, a color or #tag filter, read-only or both ways) and kept in step by `graview serve`, proven against Google itself.
- Twelve controls covered by another were fixed, and graview.dev shows the inline AI and gains this page.
- **Fewer presses to add a record.** A list's Add button now stands beside its heading, so making a record from the keyboard on the pages takes 10–14 presses where it took 17–22.
- **The GPU only where clicks land.** A Chrome whose capture build would hit-test where a view was laid out rather than where it was drawn now draws on the DOM path, so a press, a screen reader and a focused field always meet what is on screen.
- **Signs, panels and embeds that stay out of the way.** A sign at the map's edge steps past a district's name, "Go to it" hands the keyboard straight on to the record it went to, a lens is drawn in the room it has from its first frame, and an embedded app draws nothing over its host page.
releases.compatibility: The old seat's input, its panel and their settings are removed, along with the routed face's own copy: `quickAsk` replaces their setting on the Shell, the pages and the embed, and `quickAskOf` reads a stored one. The full list of removed names is in the changelog. The Shell's and the embed's `renderer` defaults to `auto`. A document's `datetime` is asked for with the date editor. The hosted page carries about 3.5 KB more up front (1.3 KB gzipped).

releases.headline: Ask with ⌘K and the right-click, be told when things happen, a faster first load, the GPU by default, and a Google calendar kept in step.
releases.summary: The quick ask and the right-click AI, notify me, a faster first load, the GPU by default, one date editor and a Google calendar kept in step, all described under 0.1.32.

releases.headline: Play an app back, link across apps, an actor that tidies, and graview.dev as a Graview app.
releases.summary:
- **Playback.** Open the app as it stood at any moment, and restore it to there.
- **Linked records.** A relation can point at a kind in another app, read there as whoever is looking.
- **An actor that tidies.** The app's own actor suggests fixes, which a person accepts or declines.
- A first look for a new app, an emoji as the app's mark, kind lists you can sort and group, navigation with filters and sections, a right-click menu on Pages and images by URL.
- Eighteen author requests and a run of scene and lens bugs fixed, a screen-reader pass, and the GPU path past 128 live views. graview.dev itself is now a Graview app.
releases.compatibility: `Store.at` and `Store.seqAt` are replaced by `pastOf` and `seqAt` on the new `@graview/core/past`. A role that removed, archived or merged other people's records only through the act that makes the kind now needs those acts named in its grant.

releases.headline: A large release of field types, list tools and data features, on a lighter page.
releases.summary:
- **New field types:** links to another app, Markdown text, phone, place and duration, and money, percent and unit formats; dates and numbers said the US way.
- **Records:** archive and merge records, lineage and provisional links, repeating dates, field-level sight, acting on several records at once, and `importRows` for bringing data in.
- **Lists:** fuzzy search, filters that scale to large lists, and cards you can read at a glance.
- `renderPlace` writes a place as static HTML, guest views can show pictures, and `store.tick` reports what changed.
- The map is laid out along the ground, and the hosted page is lighter up front than 0.1.28 despite everything added.
releases.compatibility: Breaking for imports: `edgeWords` and `valueWords` move to `@graview/core/words`, and the address helpers (`withShown`, `withQuery` and the rest) move out of `@graview/layout`; nothing is aliased. The scene's map is laid out anew, so a `sceneThumbnail` draws a different picture. Ops, stored formats, the wire and tool schemas are unchanged.

releases.headline: The people kind, grants and sights are named edits.
releases.summary: `editDocument` gains `set-people`, `add-grant`, `remove-grant`, `add-sight` and `remove-sight`, so who may do and see what can be changed as a named, previewed edit instead of a raw patch. Each is previewed in words and refused with the checker's own codes.
releases.compatibility: Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document format and check codes are unchanged. The edit vocabulary gains five ops, and an edit's refusal can now carry a specific code where every refusal was `edit`.

releases.headline: People in a document, bounded seat reads, and links that say why they did not go.
releases.summary:
- A document can name the kind that stands for its people, and its acts can say `$me` for the person acting.
- A grant can hold to your own end of a link, and a sight can reach the records that link to you.
- A seat's reads are bounded, and a worker view's link or navigate says why it did not go.
releases.compatibility: Breaking: `answerSeenBy` moved to its own entry, the read tools' answer shapes changed, `useSeatConversation` requires `said`, and `$me` is reserved as an argument name.

releases.headline: Pictures and files on records, and a failed AI turn says why.
releases.summary: A kind can carry pictures and documents: `imageField()`, `fileField()`, the image block, and uploads through the host's files seam. When a host's AI turn fails, the seat shows the host's own explanation.
releases.compatibility: Breaking for imports only: the form helpers (`formFields` and its neighbors) moved to their own entry. Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document format and tool schemas are unchanged.

releases.headline: The app on a phone: the seat closes and the screen fills.
releases.summary: On a phone, the open seat is put away by its close button, a tap on its grab line or a pull down, and the keyboard goes with it. An app fills the phone after it rotates.
releases.compatibility: Tool schemas move to `@graview/core/json-schema`.

releases.headline: Every seat judged over what it sees, problems that open on their fix, and a fit on the smallest phone.
releases.summary:
- What a seat is told is worked out over what that seat can see.
- Pressing a problem opens its repairs, wherever the record sits, and a record is renamed by pressing its name.
- The bar and the home's counts fit a 320-pixel phone at the largest text size.
- Names, yes-or-no fields and facts read in plain words. Also sync fixes.
releases.compatibility: Ops, stored formats, the wire, the declaration, check codes and tool schemas are unchanged; only where some types are declared moved.

releases.headline: The seat's turn, without the weight.
releases.summary: `turnThroughMessages` has its own entry, `@graview/tools/turn`, under 2 KB, so a host can wire the seat's turn up front without loading the whole tools package on first paint.

releases.headline: Preview and doctor, typed documents, and a seat that reads before it answers.
releases.summary:
- `graview preview` serves a document and a seed with Graview's own faces over them, no product needed, and `graview shots` photographs places headless.
- `graview doctor` says whether a product is on one Graview release.
- Documents are typed from the editor to the face, can declare facts about the whole graph, and give kinds a natural time and author field. Declared blocks have stable keys.
- The seat reads records with tools before it answers, the sync engine resolves conflicts as it is told, and kinds with no records fold into More.
- A security and correctness review of 0.1.21.

releases.headline: Who's here on every bar, axe-clean markup, and a way back in the scene.
releases.summary:
- Who else is here shows on the bar on both faces and on a phone.
- The framework's own markup passes axe-core for WCAG 2.0 to 2.2 A and AA, at desktop and phone widths, light and dark.
- The scene gets its own way back, and the overview has an address that survives a server round trip.
- A broken rule states its values to a host that reads only its message, and a read-only role is no longer warned for doing nothing.
releases.compatibility: Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document and compiled formats, check codes and tool schemas are unchanged; some presence and test-id behavior a harness reads moved.

releases.headline: List pages lead with their records, and rules read like sentences.
releases.summary:
- A list page puts its records first instead of a tall header of title and related links.
- A rule written in the rule language says its shape in plain words.
- An agent opening a new product finds what to read at the root.
- Fixed: a connect that replaces now replaces the right link, one mistake gives one check finding, and the scene from an empty address lands where the scene opens.
releases.compatibility: Additive: the document format gains an optional `pages.primary`, and check gains two warnings about it. Which places stand on the bar changed.

releases.headline: The seat floats, takes you where you ask, and draws views you can keep.
releases.summary:
- The seat is no longer a rail down the scene's edge: it floats, quietly, on both faces.
- Ask it to go somewhere and it goes, matching the request against what the declaration and the graph already name, without a model.
- Ask it for a way of seeing and it drafts a view that can be kept as a lens. Who-and-when questions are answered from the graph with no model.
- The host chooses the AI once, instead of the reader picking from a menu. The whole-page shell wears the one app bar, and the hosted page carries 9.5 KB less before the app draws.
releases.compatibility: Breaking for the components and API a host's seat reaches: the `Companion` family is removed for the floating seat and `HostAi`. Ops, stored formats, the wire, the document format and tool schemas are unchanged.

releases.headline: A lens picker in the scene, and prose that reads like prose.
releases.summary: The scene gets its own place control. A selected record is drawn once. Long text keeps its paragraphs. Parts that fail to load retry safely (`@graview/core/retry`), and no import cycles run at load time.

releases.headline: Graview's identity, and Scene and Pages side by side.
releases.summary: The framework's own look follows the third revision of its design kit and is exported as data. The scene and the pages read as two things on the bar.

releases.headline: One app bar, and brands you can edit by name.
releases.summary: One bar on every face, with the scene as a place beside the others. Named acts for an app's name and brand, contrast refusals that name the failing pair of colors, icon-sized app pictures, and search results that carry their address. The framework now spells in American English.
releases.compatibility: Breaking: names spelled the British way are renamed with no aliases (`normalize`, `summarize`, `humanizeField`, `colorsIn` and others). The undo dock is a fixed popover rather than a box in the page's flow.

releases.headline: Clearer refusals, one problem count.
releases.summary: Refusals that come from a rule now say so. The number of problems appears in one place. A host can hand the page an already compiled app.
releases.compatibility: Breaking for a caller that sent an act an argument it does not declare: it was dropped and the act ran; now it is refused as `invalid`, naming what the act takes.

releases.headline: Ranges, derived edits and fewer pills.
releases.summary: Number fields declare their ranges. A derived edit per kind covers every field nothing else sets, and refuses what it cannot take. A design pass, from building a real product, took words out of capsules.
releases.compatibility: The arrangement functions moved from `@graview/core` to `@graview/core/arrange`. From 0.1.13: `@graview/react/provider` no longer exports `UrlSync`, `useUrlSync` or `adjustment` (`@graview/react` still does).

releases.headline: Status-board moves and an address bar for the routed face.
releases.summary: A status board's columns say which lens they are in, and an act that sets the board's field is offered as a move. Scene thumbnails can be fitted to what stands. A host whose page is the app can give the routed face the browser's address bar.

releases.headline: A lighter hosted page: the checker and the seat's tools leave the main entry.
releases.summary: What only a fetched face, an agent's seat or the checker uses moved out of `@graview/core`'s main entry into subpaths named for what they hold, so a hosted page loads less up front.
releases.compatibility: Breaking for imports, with no aliases: `checkApp`, `formatFindings`, `describeApp` and the docs generators move to `@graview/core/check`, and other names to their own subpaths. From 0.1.11: `@graview/primitives/frame` exports `themeBaseCss` in place of `themeCss`, and a worker view's failure reads `start` where it read `refused`.

releases.headline: A status board lens, currencies, and set walks in the rule language.
releases.summary: A shipped `columns` lens draws a kind's records as a status board. Money fields take a currency, and the app has a default one. Figure labels are templates. The rule language walks a relation from every member of a set. The checker warns when an act reads a kind a role may not see.

releases.headline: Declared lenses and homes, and worker views you can trust with HTML.
releases.summary:
- A lens, a home view and the arrangement of pages declared in a document now draw, and a view can list related records.
- The rule language computes what pages need (sums over expressions, sorting), and kinds can declare computed fields.
- A worker view can draw HTML, SVG and CSS with nothing able to fetch or leave its region; it needs no build, is a named place with a manifest the host enforces, stops past its limits, and can be run once headless to say what it drew.
- `describePlace` says what one place shows one seat, without a browser. Every new document feature has an edit.
releases.compatibility: Additive within the document format and check codes. The guest-view protocol gains messages; derived tools gain one read tool, `describe_place`.

releases.headline: A host speaks in the app's own notices, menus and pictures.
releases.summary: A host can show its notices in the app's own voice, put its own actions in the profile menu, and draw a picture of an app without a browser. Every popover opens above everything else and behaves the same way, and the seat's rail can be put away.

releases.headline: Guest views run in a worker, for chats that cannot nest a frame.
releases.summary: A guest view can run in a worker as well as a frame, hardened before guest code runs and built as one classic script. The component kit it draws with is declared once and the host draws nothing else. A host says where its links may go, and a guest that stops answering is stopped.

releases.headline: A read-only app says so.
releases.summary: An open page is told that the app takes no changes for now, and why. An op that names a missing record is served as it is.

releases.headline: A host's refusals in its own words, and an embed that keeps to its box.
releases.summary: A host can refuse a change in its own words, an Apply with nothing changed asks the host nothing, and the embed's stylesheet stays inside its element.

releases.headline: The studio in a host's page, and half the weight.
releases.summary: A field changes in place in the studio, the host decides who is offered the studio and can refuse a change, and what the studio will not change is said up front. A hosted page carries 536 KB up front instead of 1,075 KB, with each face fetched as it is first drawn, and the framework builds its schemas in zod/mini.

releases.headline: Security: a seat learns nothing about records it may not see.
releases.summary:
- A seat is never served the id of a hidden record, and no refusal, sentence or checkpoint reveals whether one exists.
- A change is acknowledged only once it is durable, a busy host's wait is read correctly, and a hibernating host can resume its sockets.
- Refusals on the wire are written for people, and the studio hands a host back a document.
releases.compatibility: The wire and live protocols narrow what a seat with sights is sent; no field is added or removed. `remove-kind` removes more of what depended on the kind.

releases.headline: A live store a host can run, observe and deploy.
releases.summary: Refusals carry a code a program can branch on, a busy host is told apart from a refusal, presence can include agents, the declaration can change under open tabs, a remote client can be observed and can catch up, and the wire says when the client and server are on different builds.
releases.compatibility: Breaking for a client that named its own channel: `via` in a call is ignored, and a client sends `x-graview-via` to a server that trusts seat headers.

releases.headline: The declaration as a document, a live wire, and guest views.
releases.summary:
- **The declaration is a document:** one JSON object that compiles into the same app `defineApp` declares, with an edit vocabulary of twenty-one operations, rules written as expressions, and templates as data.
- **A live wire:** `openRemote({ live: true })` pushes every op to every browser as it lands, MCP is served over HTTP, and logs can be folded and compacted.
- **Guest views:** `@graview/guest`, a view somebody else wrote, in a sandboxed frame that can only ask.
- A SQL adapter, stored formats that carry their version, a conformance kit, and `docs/stability.md`, the promise a version keeps.
releases.compatibility: Breaking: a store served without `seatOf` answers 401 until it passes `trustSeatHeaders: true`, `graview serve` binds 127.0.0.1, a host's `seatOf` receives a web `Request`, a full palette needs the `good` and `bad` tokens, and a kind no sight names is seen only by the system.

releases.headline: A record read whole, in its own words.
releases.summary: A kind declares what a glance at one says, forms and lists say values in the record's words, lists narrow by numbers and words, and a policy says who may see what as well as who may do it.

releases.headline: The first public release of the framework on npm.
releases.summary: Graview's first release to npm: a framework where a typed context graph is the interface rather than the backing store. One declaration per kind drives the layout, the legal actions, the agent tools and the accessibility labels. `graview` is the tool and `@graview/*` the framework, all at one version, under the Elastic License 2.0.

releases.headline: The work before the first public release.
releases.summary: It was numbered once in the repository and never published.
